canonicalCards.rationale: The word “changes tone note to note” describes a perception, not a measured cause. The first job is to discover whether the source, processing, or surrounding arrangement produces it.
canonicalCards.recommendedFirstExperiment: Mark the exact words that change and compare mic distance/waveform level; use phrase-specific automation or dynamic control instead of a broad permanent EQ.
stopOrUndo: Stop or back off as soon as trying to make every vowel identical can make the performance unnatural.
Bypass or delete the temporary EQ band, restore the previous plug-in state, and compare against the raw capture.
canonicalCards.teachingPrinciple: A production adjective is a clue. Use one reversible test to identify the cause before prescribing the processor.
canonicalCards.title: Diagnosing a changes tone note to note vocal
tradeoffs: Trying to make every vowel identical can make the performance unnatural.
A visually impressive EQ curve is not evidence that the vocal improved.

contradictions.summary: Automatic region quantization is efficient for stable transient material. / Manual section edits reduce artifacts and preserve already-good timing.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Test a short duplicate before processing the entire track.
contradictions.whatDecides: Source complexity, Flex algorithm, amount of correction, and artifact tolerance.

contradictions.summary: Region quantization is fast and consistent across repeated patterns. / Manual edits preserve intentional timing and target only real mistakes.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use automatic correction only after a short representative test.
contradictions.whatDecides: Number of errors, consistency of pattern, ornaments, and artifact risk.

contradictions.summary: Full correction is appropriate for deliberately grid-locked material. / Partial Q-Strength/Q-Range preserves human variation.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Start partial and increase until the problem stops distracting.
contradictions.whatDecides: Material role, performance quality, genre, and desired feel.

contradictions.summary: A straight grid gives clarity and predictable structure. / A groove template or retained microtiming may better match the musical pocket.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Choose the timing authority before moving notes.
contradictions.whatDecides: Genre, reference part, arrangement, and whether off-grid timing is intentional.

contradictions.summary: Quantize/Flex the performance to a fixed production grid. / Build a tempo map so programmed parts follow the expressive performance.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Preserve the original and test both in a project alternative.
contradictions.whatDecides: Artistic rubato, later sequencing needs, genre, and editing complexity.

contradictions.summary: Small randomization can break sterile repetition. / Randomness can create sloppiness without musical phrasing.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Prefer retained performance or groove template; use bounded randomization sparingly.
contradictions.whatDecides: Pattern, role, amount, velocity/timing constraints, and reference groove.

contradictions.summary: Smart preserves relative ordering and expressive internal relationships. / Classic provides direct grid locking and can be more predictable for simple rhythmic material.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: A/B duplicate regions; do not make Smart the universal default.
contradictions.whatDecides: Arpeggios, pedal/CC data, flams, desired correction, and event complexity.

contradictions.summary: Compression provides short-term control and density. / Manual/recorded rides place phrases and syllables more musically.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Use clip gain, moderate compression, and automation as complementary rather than exclusive.
contradictions.whatDecides: Time scale of the problem. Extreme local outliers, short-term envelope, and section-level placement need different tools.

contradictions.summary: A de-esser gives consistent dynamic frequency control. / Manual clip gain/automation can be more transparent for isolated or highly variable consonants.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Calibrate DeEsser 2 conservatively and use local edits for outliers.
contradictions.whatDecides: How frequent and consistent the sibilance is, and whether automated reduction causes lisping/darkness.

contradictions.summary: Sends provide independent wet processing, sharing, filtering, and automation. / Insert effects are valid for deliberate serial transformations or simple self-contained chains.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Default to wet aux for conventional mix effects but explain exceptions.
contradictions.whatDecides: Need for independent dry level, shared space, automation, and creative topology.

contradictions.summary: Solo helps locate noise, resonances, and edit artifacts. / Full-mix context decides balance, masking, and whether a tonal change is useful.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Move between views deliberately; never finalize context-dependent EQ in solo alone.
contradictions.whatDecides: Diagnostic stage. Use solo to inspect, context to decide.

contradictions.summary: High-pass filtering can remove rumble, plosives, and unnecessary low energy. / Aggressive filtering can remove chest, warmth, and low-register identity.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Raise cutoff while listening in context, then back off; do not provide one universal frequency.
contradictions.whatDecides: Singer, mic distance, lowest notes, arrangement, and whether low energy is actually problematic.

contradictions.summary: One well-set compressor is simpler and easier to diagnose. / Two modest stages with distinct jobs can sound smoother than one stage doing heavy work.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Require each stage to have a named job and level-match the alternatives.
contradictions.whatDecides: Peak behavior, leveling need, desired color, and total accumulated gain reduction.

contradictions.summary: Use delay or short filtered ambience to preserve intelligibility and avoid a washed lead. / Reverb is a normal and valuable vocal tool when decay, predelay, filtering, and level fit the song.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Do not forbid either tool. Offer a level-matched A/B with separate wet auxes.
contradictions.whatDecides: Arrangement density, genre, desired depth, phrase spacing, and whether the effect masks consonants.

contradictions.summary: Multiple real takes can create density and width. / A strong single lead often preserves clarity, intimacy, and emotional focus better.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Compare one, two, and three takes at matched total loudness; never call triple tracking universally professional.
contradictions.whatDecides: Performance consistency, genre, desired scale, lyric intelligibility, and arrangement.

contradictions.summary: Source changes can solve performance, plosive, room, and mic-position problems cleanly. / Editing/restoration is appropriate when the performance is irreplaceable or re-recording is impossible.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Run a short re-record test before a large repair workflow when feasible.
contradictions.whatDecides: Artistic value of take, artifact severity, time, repeatability, and repair transparency.

contradictions.summary: Stronger correction can meet a polished genre expectation. / Selective correction preserves vibrato, drift, and identity.
contradictions.tutorBehavior: Start selective; compare corrected and original phrases, not only blobs.
contradictions.whatDecides: Genre, performance, desired aesthetic, artifact audibility, and emotional role.
